newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says fiercest sandstorm in 30 years killed 18.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says fiercest sandstorm in 30 years killed 18.

text.p: Eighteen people died in accidents ranging from fallen trees to collapsed walls when the strongest sandstorm in 30 years hit Egypt on Friday.

The interior ministry said in a statement on Saturday the 18 dead included a three-year-old child. It said 12 provinces were affected by the storm, which sparked fires by downing electricity cables and ripped street billboards off their posts.
A farmer was crushed by a fallen mulberry tree in his fields.
"I thought it was the Day of Judgment," an old man told the Egyptian newspaper Akhbar al-Youm.
The storm disrupted air traffic at Cairo International Airport and plunged Cairo into darkness for about one hour.
Meteorological Authority chairman Abdul Moneim Abdul Rahman said on Friday winds reached 110 km (68 miles) per hour, making it the strongest storm in Egypt for at least 30 years.
Sandstorms usually hit Egypt this time of the year. They are called Khamasin (fifty) because they blow intermittently for about 50 days.
